title: Officer faced life-or-death struggle with mentally ill man
article: A Vancouver police officer repeatedly stabbed in the chest and arms by a man suffering from paranoid schizophrenia described Wednesday a life-and-death struggle that ended when the man was fatally shot by another police officer.

Const. Craig Look was testifying at a coroner's inquest into the death of Dean Nicholas Andrusyk, whose life ended at age 49 after a late-night altercation in September 2004 with Look and his partner, Const. John Filippelli.

Look, then a rookie with about one year of police experience, and Filippelli, a police officer for three years, were sent to 41st and Victoria to talk to the victim of a domestic dispute. The 911 caller -- a man who sounded drunk and upset -- claimed his girlfriend had hit him on the legs with a hockey stick.
When the two uniformed officers arrived at the intersection in their police cruiser, they saw a man sitting on a bench beside a bus stop near the intersection.
Look told a five-person coroner's jury that the man aimed his hand towards him like it was a gun and pulled his trigger finger back as if he was going to shoot them.
At that point, Look said, he assumed Andrusyk was the male complainant who had called police, but "instead of a handshake, we're greeted with a finger trigger pull and an annoying face."

Look, who was sitting in the front passenger seat, said Andrusyk got up from the bench and stood close to the passenger door of their police cruiser, preventing Look from leaving the vehicle. Look said he directed Andrusyk to move away from the door, but Andrusyk remained where he was, saying loudly: "You don't have the right to tell me what to do!"

At that point, Look said, he leaned into the car and used a leg to kick the door open so he could get out of the vehicle. But when Look stepped out and on to the pavement, he found himself trapped between Andrusyk and the open door. Look said he yelled, "Get back, get back!" but Andrusyk wouldn't move away and Andrusyk began striking at his chest.
Look, who was wearing a bullet-resistant Kevlar vest and heavy metal chest plate to protect his vital organs, felt two blows on his chest.
"I thought he was just hitting me," he said.

Moments later -- Look said he guessed the entire altercation lasted between 15 and 30 seconds -- Look felt a "hot burning sensation" on his right wrist. He then saw a sharp metal object in Andrusyk's hand -- a drywall saw -- and yelled out to Filippelli: "Jesus Christ! He's stabbing me!"
Two civilian witnesses who happened to be on the sidewalk both testified that they heard the officers shout out warnings before Andrusyk was shot.
Filippelli confirmed he fired a single bullet at Andrusyk.
"I feared for my life and the life of my partner," Filippelli said.

Dr. Charles Lee, the forensic pathologist who conducted the autopsy, said Andrusyk died of a single gun shot wound. Post-mortem tests found no traces of alcohol or drugs -- including the drugs Andrusyk was supposed to be using to control his mental illness.
